description: Target schema for the JDBC test-fixture MySQL table appdb.customers - full_name split into first_name and last_name. Same schema_name as v1 so the two are versions of one schema rather than two unrelated schemas.

fields.name: customer_id
fields.description: Unique customer identifier. Maps from the source column 'id'.

fields.name: email_address
fields.description: Customer email address. Maps from the source column 'email'.

fields.name: first_name
fields.description: Customer given name. Derived from the FIRST whitespace-separated token of the source column 'name'. The source has no separate given-name column.

fields.name: last_name
fields.description: Customer family name. Derived from the REMAINDER of the source column 'name' after the first whitespace-separated token. The source has no separate family-name column.

fields.name: registration_date
fields.description: Date the customer registered. Maps from the source column 'created_at', which is a TIMESTAMP and must be narrowed to a date.

fields.name: region_code
fields.description: Customer region. Maps from the source column 'region'. The fixture data cycles through exactly these four values.

fields.name: account_status
fields.description: Account status. NO source column supplies this — appdb.customers has no status column. Present on purpose to exercise the unsourced-target-field path.

change_log.changes: Initial schema - every field renamed relative to the source
Split full_name into first_name and last_name. One source column now feeds two required target fields, which is a transform rather than a rename.
